text:
## Observations

1. The score increases with each of its three arguments because every sequence entry is positive.
2. After sorting the sequences in descending order, each index triple other than \((0,0,0)\) has a unique parent obtained by decreasing its first nonzero index by one. The parent’s score is at least the child’s score.
3. Every index triple counts separately, even when several triples have the same score.
4. Only the first \(K\) triples in descending score order are needed, and \(K\) is at most \(5\times10^5\).

## Solution sketch

> The score increases with each of its three arguments because every sequence entry is positive.

1. Sort all three sequences in descending order and use zero-based indices. The triple \((0,0,0)\) has a maximum score, so put it in a max-heap keyed by score.

> After sorting the sequences in descending order, each index triple other than \((0,0,0)\) has a unique parent obtained by decreasing its first nonzero index by one. The parent’s score is at least the child’s score.

2. Pop the triple \((i,j,k)\) with the highest score. Generate its children by increasing \(i\), by increasing \(j\) if \(i=0\), and by increasing \(k\) if \(i=j=0\). Skip any child with an index equal to \(N\). Compute each remaining child’s score and push it into the heap. Each triple has one parent, so it enters the heap at most once. For any unpopped triple, the first unpopped triple on its path from the root is already in the heap and has a score at least as large. Therefore each pop returns a maximum among all remaining triples.

> Every index triple counts separately, even when several triples have the same score.

3. Count every pop toward \(K\) and print the score of the \(K\)-th pop. Ties can be popped in any order. This handles repeated entries and all-equal sequences. When \(K=1\), the initial triple is the answer, including the case \(N=1\). When \(K=N^3\), the last pop gives the minimum score.

> Only the first \(K\) triples in descending score order are needed, and \(K\) is at most \(5\times10^5\).

4. Stop immediately after the \(K\)-th pop. Each earlier pop adds at most three entries, so heap processing takes \(O(K\log(K+1))\) time and \(O(K)\) space. Sorting takes \(O(N\log N)\) time, and total space including the input sequences is \(O(N+K)\).

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
